Subject: Aurelia POC — recap and next steps

Hi Julia —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment going into the hands-on POC: 

Summary of needs we heard
- Primary workload: multi-turn clinical note summarization and extraction (avg turn length ~450 tokens, peak 2.5k).
- Quality sensitivity: hallucination on “medication_change” entities is a showstopper — desired recall >= 95% on the eval set you shared.
- Latency targets: sub-400ms for single-turn inference in dedicated mode, tolerant of higher tail for very long contexts.
- Compliance: logs/audit retention required for 12 months.

Recommended evaluation plan (what we will deliver this week)
1) Prompt set + eval harness: see attached aurelia_promptset_v1.csv and the shared eval harness link.
2) Baseline models to run: Mistral-Instruct-30B, Llama2-70B-chat (non-finetuned), Falcon-40B-instruct.
3) Quant/throughput matrix: run AWQ-4 and GPTQ-4 on the most promising checkpoints; include one FP8 run for throughput exploration.
4) Acceptance criteria: maintain entity recall >= 95% on eval set while achieving >=1.2x token/s uplift vs your current server.

Immediate asks from your side
- Confirm the final prompt permutations in the attached CSV (highlight any 1–2 golden prompts).
- Share a labeled sample of the hallucination cases (anonymized) if possible.

Attachments and links
- aurelia_promptset_v1.csv (attached)
- aurelia_eval_summary_v1.pdf (initial baseline we've run on a small dev slice)
- Drive: https://drive.redwood.example.com/aurelia/poc/eval-summary
- HubSpot deal: https://hubspot.example.com/deal/12345678

Next logistics
- We’ll drop a set of short benchmarking runs today (AWQ-4 + GPTQ-4) and send a quick note with observed latency/throughput and any quality deltas.
- Proposed follow-up: Wed 3/17 10:00am PT for results review and decision on which quant path to scale.

Thanks — looking forward.

— Vivek

Subject: Re: Aurelia POC — AWQ/GPTQ/FP8 quick trade study and recommended configs

Hi Julia, Vivek —

Quick technical readout from the initial micro-benchmarks we ran overnight on the dev slice you provided. I focused on the Mistral-Instruct-30B checkpoint since it hit the recall bar best in float32. Notes below are intentionally concise — we’ll expand in the Wed review.

Experimental setup (short)- Hardware: Dedicated spot on g5.48xlarge-like with A10G profiler; later runs on A100-80GB for FP8.
- Sequence profile: 450 tokens average, 2.5k peak.
- Metrics: entity recall (our annotated set), exact-match extraction, median latency, 95th pct latency, tokens/sec.

Summary of results (AWQ-4 vs GPTQ-4 vs float32)
- Float32 baseline (Mistral-30B): recall 96.8%, median latency 320ms, tokens/sec = 1.0x (baseline).
- AWQ-4: recall 95.4% (−1.4 pts), median latency 230ms (≈1.4x token/s), 95th pct latency improved by ~20%.
- GPTQ-4: recall 96.1% (−0.7 pts), median latency 260ms (≈1.2x token/s), more stable recall on long-context prompts.
- FP8 (early): recall 95.0% (−1.8 pts), median latency 200ms (≈1.6x token/s), tooling still experimental — some ops fallback to FP16 which reduced predicted savings.

Interpretation and recommendation
- If your priority is strictly meeting the 95% recall bar and maximizing throughput conservatively, GPTQ-4 is the safest first step (smaller delta vs float32, more predictable on edge-case prompts).
- AWQ-4 gives the best latency/throughput uplift with a modest recall hit — it may be acceptable if we can tune prompts or apply a small lightweight reranker on extracted meds to recover recall.
- FP8 is attractive for instance class downsizing but needs more engineering time (kernel maturity and some accuracy instability on very long contexts).

Suggested immediate plan
1) Run a GPTQ-4 full eval across the golden prompts (rows 2, 7, 11) + hallucination cases this afternoon.
2) Parallel AWQ-4 run on a narrower slice (top-k prompts) to quantify whether a reranker recovers the −1.4pt recall.
3) If both pass the 95% threshold on golden prompts, iterate on cost modeling and instance sizing for a Dedicated proposal.

Attachments: awq_vs_gptq_notes.md (high level run notes), we also pushed an updated aurelia_eval_summary_v1.pdf to the drive link.

Happy to walk through the numbers on Wed; I can share the raw CSV of per-example diffs if you want to dig in.

— Camila
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
